task.description: Independently re-verify REQ-206's 6 acceptance criteria before DOC-UPDATER marks it done. Re-run tests, re-check scenario fixture disclosure headers, re-confirm the Runner extension is additive, re-verify the two UNIMPLEMENTED findings, and confirm the R-Co scenario-corpus follow-up recommendation reaches ORCH.

result.summary: All 6 REQ-206 acceptance criteria independently re-derived as genuinely met from real command output and source inspection, not from trusting step-02a/step-04's self-reports. One caveat carried forward for ORCH (not a blocker): the design-stage recommendation to file a follow-up issue mirroring ISS-0388 (port real R-Co tests/simulation/scenarios/*.yaml scenario content once R-Co access is available) exists only in lib/letflow/design/req206-swiftroute-scenario-execution.md and step-01/step-01b handoffs -- it was NOT carried into step-02a's result.issues or any later handoff. Re-elevated here so ORCH acts on it at Step 6/Final, same mechanism REQ-205's own RELEASE-VALIDATOR used for its AC1 caveat.

Also ran mix test test/fixtures/simulation/fixture_shape_test.exs (adjacent fixture-shape coverage) -- passed.
independent_verification.runner_diff_is_additive: git diff origin/main...HEAD -- test/support/simulation/runner.ex reviewed line-by-line: every change is a new struct field with a safe default (unbuilt_feature: nil, disposition: :executed, severity: nil, notes: nil), a widened type union (:api | :gui -> + :skip), a new leading run/1 clause for unbuilt_feature that short-circuits before any existing logic, and a new :skip case branch in the step-dispatch cond/case. No existing branch's behavior was deleted or altered in a way the still-passing 15 pre-existing tests would not have caught.
independent_verification.advance_timer_grep: grep -rn 'advance-timer|advance_timer' lib/letflow/router.ex lib/letflow/routers/ -> zero matches (exit 1), re-run myself independently of step-02a's claim -- confirms the AC3 finding is factually accurate as of this commit.
independent_verification.attachment_grep: grep -rln 'attach|document' lib/letflow/routers/*.ex -> hits in 10 files, all manually inspected: every match is either 'problem document' (RFC 9457 error body terminology), 'documented' (doc comments), or SolutionPack's unrelated 'pack document'/'attaches variable schemas to a pre-existing [definition]' usage -- zero actual attachment/document-upload route or handler for shipment delivery notes. Confirms the AC4 finding is factually accurate.
independent_verification.scenario_yaml_disclosure_headers: Read all 4 files under test/fixtures/simulation/swiftroute/scenarios/ -- each opens with a '# Synthetic --' header naming the exact unreachable R-Co source path and cross-referencing the design doc's §0, matching REQ-205's own established disclosure convention (verified against test/fixtures/simulation/swiftroute/company.yaml's '# Ported from R-Co ... (ISS-0388)' header for contrast -- the scenario files correctly use the synthetic-disclosure wording, not the ported wording, because the underlying scenario corpus is still unreachable, unlike the now-real company/org/process fixtures).
independent_verification.findings_reported_correctly: step-02a-elixir-dev.json's result.issues carries exactly 2 entries: 'POST /api/v1/instances/:id/advance-timer does not exist' (severity MINOR, matches scenario's own documented SKIP/MINOR fallback) and 'No document/attachment API exists in Letflow or in R-Co's own src/' (severity MINOR) -- both with affected_files and evidence descriptions; neither fabricated (both independently re-confirmed by grep above) nor silently dropped.

caveat.title: R-Co scenario-corpus-porting follow-up (mirrors ISS-0388) present only in the design doc, not carried into any post-design handoff
caveat.detail: lib/letflow/design/req206-swiftroute-scenario-execution.md (§0) and handoffs/WF02-REQ206-20260901/step-01-code-designer-rework1.json's recommendation_for_orch both explicitly recommend ORCH file a follow-up issue at Step 6/Final -- same shape as docs/issues/ISS-0388.yaml (discovered_by: RELEASE-VALIDATOR, tags: [fixture-porting, needs-r-co-access, s7], affected_files: the 4 scenario YAMLs under test/fixtures/simulation/swiftroute/scenarios/, related: [REQ-206]) -- so a future session/host with genuine R-Co filesystem access can port the real tests/simulation/scenarios/*.yaml scenario content, the same way ISS-0388 fixed REQ-205's company/org/process fixtures. Grepped step-02a/02c/02d/03/03b/04 for this recommendation: zero mentions past step-01b. It did not get lost through negligence -- REQ-205's own precedent (see handoffs/WF02-REQ205-20260831/release-validation-report-20260831.md) shows RELEASE-VALIDATOR itself, not ELIXIR-DEV, is this pipeline's established vehicle for surfacing this class of recommendation to ORCH at Step 6. Re-stating it here closes that gap rather than letting it fall through silently.
caveat.downstream_consequence_if_not_acted_on: Without this follow-up issue filed, REQ-206's 4 scenario YAMLs remain self-authored synthetic content indefinitely (not a correctness problem for REQ-206 itself -- disclosed, structurally faithful, and does not block REQ-206 being done -- but a real content gap: REQ-207/REQ-208's Vortex/Meridian scenario corpora will face the identical unreachable-R-Co-scenario-corpus situation, and without this issue on record, that gap risks being silently re-discovered and re-justified from scratch by each of REQ-207/REQ-208 instead of being centrally tracked and resolved once.
caveat.does_this_block_marking_REQ-206_done: No. Same reasoning as REQ-205's AC1 caveat: the requirement's mechanism, tests, and disclosure are all genuinely correct and independently verified; only the literal byte-for-byte R-Co scenario content is unavailable, and that unavailability is disclosed everywhere it appears (file headers, design doc, this report). ACCEPT WITH RECORDED CAVEAT.
caveat.action_requested_of_orch: File a follow-up issue via letflow-queue at Step 6/Final mirroring docs/issues/ISS-0388.yaml's shape, per the design doc's §0 recommendation and step-01-code-designer-rework1.json's recommendation_for_orch field, and make it visible for REQ-207/REQ-208 to reference rather than re-deriving independently.

result.next_action: Route to DOC-UPDATER (Step 6) to flip REQ-206 status to done, record AC1-6 all PASS (no partial-met ACs, unlike REQ-205), and cross-reference this report's caveat and the requested ISS-0388-mirroring follow-up issue in the run-history event. ORCH should also file that follow-up issue at Step 6/Final per the design doc's own recommendation.
